hints.content:
###The strategy

The perimeter of a hexagon is the sum of the lengths of all the sides. 

Note that $FA=BC$ and $CD=EF$, so we only need to find the lengths of $\overline{AB}$, $\overline{BC}$, $\overline{CD}$, and $\overline{DE}$.

Some sides are perfectly horizontal. We can find those lengths using just the $x$-coordinates of the endpoints of those sides.

We can find the length of sides $\overline{BC}$ and $\overline{CD}$ using the Pythagorean theorem (or the distance formula).

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Hexagon A B C D E F has point A at negative six, nine, point B at five, nine, point C at eight, one, point D at two, negative six, point E negative three, negative six, and point F at negative nine, one. Sides C D and E F are congruent. Sides A F and B C are congruent. A horizontal highlighted line of three units connects from point B to a highlighted vertical line of eight units to point C.

hints.content:
###Step 2: Finding the length $CD$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
CD^2&= \redE{6}^2 +\redE{7}^2  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
CD&= \sqrt{\redE{6}^2 +\redE{7}^2 }   &&\text{Square root both sides} \\\\
&=\goldE{\sqrt{85}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Hexagon A B C D E F has point A at negative six, nine, point B at five, nine, point C at eight, one, point D at two, negative six, point E negative three, negative six, and point F at negative nine, one. Sides C D and E F are congruent. Sides A F and B C are congruent. A horizontal highlighted line of six units connects from point D to a highlighted vertical line of seven units to point C.

hints.content:
###Step 3: Finding the horizontal lengths

If a side is horizontal, we can use the $x$-coordinates of its endpoints to find its length.

* $\overline{AB}$ is $11$ units long
* $\overline{DE}$ is $5$ units long

###The answer

The exact perimeter of hexagon $ABCDEF$ is $16+2\sqrt{73}+2\sqrt{85}$ units (approximately $51.5$ units).
